newsitem.title: CANADA: Half of Saskatchewan wheat crop in heading stage.
newsitem.headline: Half of Saskatchewan wheat crop in heading stage.

text.p: Half of Saskatchewan's wheat crop was in the heading stage, ahead of the five-year average, Saskatchewan Agriculture said in its crop report.

Fifty five percent of spring cereals were at or past the heading stage compared to the average 30 percent. Forty percent of flax was past the flowering stage compared with the average of 20 percent. Eighty percent of canola was at or past the flowering stage compared to the average of 60 percent. Eighty percent of fall cereals were in the dough stage versus the average of 72 percent. Pulse crops were 76 percent past flowering compared to 37 percent last week.

Drought, hail and wheat midge were the main causes of crop damage in the past week. Wind and hail were seen throughout all of the east and some west central areas. Spraying for wheat midge began in the southern and central areas.
Soil moisture deteriorated across Saskatchewan in the past week, particularly in the southern grainbelt. Rain was needed in many areas to sustain crop growth and development.

An average 11 mm (0.4 inch) of rain fell on the southern grainbelt with up to 50 mm (2 inches) near Carnduff, Oxbow and Stoughton. Drought damage was reported in almost every crop district and topsoil moisture deteriorated substantially.

Central Saskatchewan reported an average of 12 mm (0.5 inch) of rain, but Quill Lake and Fosston saw 50 mm (2 inches). Hail damage of up to 100 percent was estimated on a two km (1.2 miles) wide strip west of Canora.
Northern districts saw an average 11 mm (0.4 inch) of rain with more than 50 mm (2 inches) near Pleasantdale. Topsoil moisture deteriorated in the past week leading to reports of drought damage.
